about: The moth's hull lines (docs/moth-2): a few curves along her length that hull_moth.py turns into sections. Frame: x forward from the hull's middle (stem +1.6775, transom -1.6775: the class's 3,355 mm), y to one side from the centreline, z up from the keel's lowest point; hull_moth.py moves z to the design waterline once it has solved where she floats. Shape read by eye from the CC BY / PD photos in refs.json (the flying broadside, the boat on her side, the two on trolleys): nothing traced. An invented hull inside the class rules, not any builder's.

keel.note: The keel line, as height above its lowest point: almost straight (a moth's hull only matters at rest and at take-off), a short, tight forefoot into a plumb stem (the afloat photo shows a tall, nearly upright bow), a little rise to the transom. Points are (x, z).

sheer.note: The deck edge's height above the keel's lowest point (x, z): highest near the bow (she noses into waves when low-riding), lower toward the transom so the sailor can sit back.

plan.note: Half-breadth at the deck edge (x, y): widest a little aft of the middle, a fine bow, a broad transom for the gantry's feet.

section.note: Each section is a V that rounds into upright topsides: half-breadth at height t (0 keel, 1 deck edge) is plan(x) * t^power, the power smaller (fuller, rounder) aft and larger (sharper V) forward. deadrise_flat rounds the keel over its lowest few cm; deck_crown is how high the deck's middle stands over its edges; edge_round the deck edge's radius.
